comment: A TYPE and an INSTANCE for it are two declarations, and this file used to offer the name `Collision` twice: `instance == Collision where …` published its container under the instance TARGET type, so the file declared `Collision` once as the type and once as the implementation. That was a PHANTOM DECLARATION and its cost is measured on the 312-file population (`validation/m14/fixtures/clean/phantom-census.mts`): 699 containers in 94 files, 93 of them named after a type the SAME file also declares for real, and 1,009 of the lane's 6,856 residual edges reachable by removing them. The container is now `Collision::instance`, kind `impl` (the Rust lane's `<target>::impl` discipline), and the file declares `Collision` exactly ONCE. THIS FIXTURE NOW PINS THE ABSENCE OF THE COLLISION rather than the dedupe that hid it: `expectSymbolCount` 1 on the bare name is the anti-regression pin — a revert to bare-target naming fails here, and so does any second declaration of `Collision`. The old dedupe in `emitExports` is kept for the invariant it enforces (one export name, one provider) and is no longer reached by this shape: `Collision::instance` is kind `impl`, which is not an exportable kind.

expectSymbols.name: Collision::instance
expectSymbols.comment: the instance container — namespaced under its target, and NOT a declaration of `Collision`
an instance-member operator is a METHOD of the instance, and its owner is still the NOMINAL type `Collision` — the container's name change moves no edge endpoint

expectSymbolCount.name: Collision
expectSymbolCount.comment: ONE declaration: the type. The instance no longer claims the bare name (it used to be 2)

expectSymbolCount.name: Collision::instance
expectSymbolCount.comment: and exactly one container, so a mutant that emits both spellings is caught

exportsNote: expectExports/forbidExports match fields EXACTLY, so no `comment` key may appear inside an entry. `Collision` is exported once, as the TYPE; the container is not exported because `impl` is not an exportable kind — the old first-wins dedupe is no longer what makes this true.

forbidExports.name: Collision
forbidExports.comment: the container is no longer a `class`, and nothing may export it under the bare name

forbidExports.name: Collision::instance
forbidExports.comment: an implementation is not part of a module's interface

expectRelationships.comment: instance_declaration: implements target-type -> class, on the `instance == Collision where` line (M59.O2 site line). The SOURCE is the target type, unchanged by the container rename — this row is why the rename is surgical rather than a re-pointing of every instance edge.
the constructor is contained by the TYPE at its own line
the TYPE at its definition line…

…and the INSTANCE container at ITS line. This pair used to read two `contains -> Collision` rows, which is exactly what a per-set dedupe would have collapsed; the two sites are now also two distinct TARGETS, so the per-site rule is observable in the targets as well as in the lines.

one containment of the container, at the instance's line

forbidRelationships.comment: THE PHANTOM, forbidden: line 17 declares an INSTANCE for `Collision`, not `Collision`. A container named after its bare target puts this row back.
